name: Labor on Chol HaMoed (Melacha b'Moed)
notes: Detailed rules governing which types of work are permitted or forbidden on the intermediate days of a Festival, including distinctions between professional and amateur work, public needs vs. private, and avoiding financial loss (davar ha'aved)

name: Davar HaAved (Preventing Financial Loss on Chol HaMoed)
notes: Principle permitting otherwise prohibited labor on Chol HaMoed when there is risk of significant financial loss; covers agricultural and commercial contexts

name: Tzorech HaMoed (Labor for Festival Needs)
notes: Category of permitted Chol HaMoed labor done specifically for the needs of the Festival itself, e.g., food preparation, obtaining clothing

name: Mourning on Chol HaMoed
notes: Rules governing mourning practices (aninut, avelut) that occur during or coincide with Chol HaMoed; includes restrictions on eulogies, rending garments, overturned bed, consolation meal

name: Festival Interrupting Mourning Period
notes: Halakhic principle that a pilgrimage festival (Pesach, Shavuot, Sukkot) interrupts and/or cancels the seven-day or thirty-day mourning period; includes rules about how many days before the festival burial must occur

name: Shiva and Shloshim (Seven and Thirty Days of Mourning)
notes: The seven-day and thirty-day mourning periods, their requirements and how they interact with Shabbat and Festivals

name: Seudat Havraah (First Mourner's Meal)
notes: The meal provided to mourners after burial by neighbors/community; rules about who provides it, what vessels may be used, and whether it applies on Chol HaMoed

name: Consolation Row (Shurah) and Mourners' Blessing
notes: Specific practice of consolers standing in a row at the cemetery to console mourners; and the recitation (or non-recitation) of birkat avelim during Chol HaMoed

name: Wailing and Lamentation (Yelalah and Kinah)
notes: Distinction between communal wailing (all together) and antiphonal lamentation (one leads, others respond); rules about when each is permitted including on Chol HaMoed, Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah, and Purim

name: Eulogy on Chol HaMoed and Other Special Days
notes: Prohibition on eulogies during Chol HaMoed; related rules about not setting down the bier in public; thirty days before Festival restriction

name: Rending Garments in Mourning (Keria)
notes: Practice of rending garments as sign of mourning; rules about when it is suspended such as during Chol HaMoed

name: Tzaraat Examination on Chol HaMoed
notes: Dispute about whether a priest may examine tzaraat symptoms during Chol HaMoed; Rabbi Meir permits lenient examination but not stringent; Rabbis prohibit both

name: Ostracism/Excommunication (Nidui) — Practical Halakhot
notes: Practical consequences of nidui including prohibition on haircutting and laundering; release from nidui on Chol HaMoed and its effects

name: Irrigation on Chol HaMoed
notes: Rules permitting irrigation from newly emerged or established springs but prohibiting use of cistern water or shadoof due to excessive labor

name: Marking Graves on Chol HaMoed
notes: Requirement to mark graves for public impurity awareness; inspectors going out to uproot kilayim; public welfare activities permitted on Chol HaMoed

name: Gathering Bones of the Deceased (Likkut Atzamot)
notes: Ancient practice of secondary burial — collecting bones from temporary grave for reburial in ancestral tomb; dispute whether permitted on Chol HaMoed due to joy vs. mourning

name: Prohibition of Marriage on Chol HaMoed
notes: Prohibition against marrying a new wife (virgin or widow) on Chol HaMoed so as not to mix one's personal joy with the joy of the Festival; remarrying divorced wife is permitted

name: Laundering Clothes on Chol HaMoed
notes: General prohibition on laundering on Chol HaMoed; exceptions for those returning from abroad, released from prison/captivity, released from nidui, zavim/zavot, yoledot, and quick-dirtying towels

name: Haircutting on Chol HaMoed
notes: General prohibition on cutting hair on Chol HaMoed; exceptions for those who could not cut hair before the Festival: returnees from abroad, released prisoners, those released from nidui/vow, nazirite, metzora

name: Writing Documents on Chol HaMoed
notes: Which legal documents may be written on Chol HaMoed (betrothal, divorce, wills, prozbul, chalitza, etc.) and which may not (loan documents, Torah scrolls, tefillin, mezuzot)

name: Prozbul
notes: Document authorizing court to collect loans despite shemitat kesafim; listed among documents that may be written on Chol HaMoed

name: Public Welfare Work on Chol HaMoed (Tzorchei Rabbim)
notes: Category of permitted labor on Chol HaMoed for communal/public needs: repairing cisterns, roads, streets, ritual baths, marking graves, uprooting kilayim

name: Shavuot's Status Regarding Mourning
notes: Dispute whether Shavuot (one-day festival) acts like Shabbat (counts but doesn't interrupt) or like other pilgrimage festivals (interrupts) for purposes of mourning period calculation

name: Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur's Status Regarding Mourning
hebrew: ראש השנה ויום כיפור לענין אבלות
notes: Dispute (Rabban Gamliel vs. Rabbis) whether Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur interrupt the mourning period like pilgrimage festivals or only count like Shabbat
